Coerce any tabular input to a plain data frame, loudly

Source: R/input_structures.R
as_linkage_table.Rd

Accepts a `data.frame` and anything that subclasses or converts to one – `tbl_df`, `data.table`, a matrix with column names – and returns a plain `data.frame`. The conversion is announced when it discards anything a caller might expect to survive, which is the point: a silent conversion is how a `data.table`'s reference semantics or an `sf` geometry column disappears between the call and the join (srr G2.7, G2.9).

Usage

as_linkage_table(x, arg = "input", quiet = FALSE)

Arguments

x

tabular input.

arg

[character(1)] the argument name, for messages.

quiet

[logical(1)] suppress the conversion message. Defaults to `FALSE`, because the message is the standard.

Value

[data.frame] a plain data frame with the same columns and rows.

Examples

as_linkage_table(data.frame(id = 1:2, surname = c("A", "B")), "roster")
#>   id surname
#> 1  1       A
#> 2  2       B
as_linkage_table(matrix(c("1", "A"), nrow = 1,
                        dimnames = list(NULL, c("id", "surname"))), "roster")
#> roster converted from matrix to data.frame: every column becomes character, because a matrix has one type
#>   id surname
#> 1  1       A
